text:
The tool output doesn't confirm that Sentinel-2 imagery was used. The 2022 loss comes from the Hansen/UMD Global Forest Change dataset (GFC-2025-v1.13), an annual series covering 2001–2025 at 30 m pixel size. That resolution is typical of Landsat-based products, not Sentinel-2, which is 10 m. The tool output doesn't name the underlying sensor, so I can't say which imagery was used.

What the evidence does show:
- Loss in 2022 was 0.6 ha, or 3.41% of the 17.6 ha asset.
- The JRC GFC2020 reference maps 100% of the event area as forest in 2020.
- Later years were observed, so the event meets the corroboration rule.

If sensor provenance matters, check the Hansen dataset's documentation or ask the engine's provider.
